newsitem.title: UK: Brit Biotech to publish lead drug data.
newsitem.headline: Brit Biotech to publish lead drug data.

text.p: Crucial data on British Biotech Plc's lead product, an injectable anti-pancreatitis drug, will overshadow the release of second-quarter results from the group on Wednesday, analysts said on Monday.

The Oxford-based research group, best known for its potentially ground-breaking anti-cancer treatment Marimastat, will publish the results of late-stage, or Phase III, trials on pancreatitis treatment Lexipafant with second-quarter figures.

The group is expected to post a pre-tax loss of around 8.0 million stg for the three months to the end of October, in line with first-quarter losses but up from a loss of 4.0 million stg a year earlier.

This reflects increased spending on the group's maturing drug pipeline, with Phase III trials of Marimastat in a range of cancers underway or in preparation. However the figures will benefit from interest payments on the group's 143 million stg rights issue completed in July.

While Marimastat is seen as the flagship drug for British Biotech and indeed the whole UK biotech sector, analysts believe Lexipafant will provide an important stream of funds for the rest of the group's pipeline.
One analyst, who asked not to be named, said "compared to Marimastat it is not as significant in product terms, but given that it is the first product to market it is a highly significant event."

Pancreatitis is currently a poorly treated condition which affects around 200,000 people a year in the U.S. alone. Around eight to 10 percent of sufferers die from the disease. Phase II trials showed Lexipafant helped to prevent kidney and liver failure and to improve organs that have already failed.

Analysts at ABN-Amro Hoare Govett, which acts as broker to British Biotech, predict peak sales for the drug of 300 million stg a year by 2010. Lehman Brothers analyst Ian Smith said he had pencilled in peak sales of around $300 million a year if the drug got to market.
"Clearly if the results are very good and the drug seems to be very effective, that could affect the price" (Lexipafant is sold for), Smith said.

British Biotech hopes positive trial results on Lexipafant will put it on track to file for regulatory approval in Europe the first quarter of 1997, with a product on the market in 1998. A parallel trial in the U.S. is currently underway.
The results to be published on Wednesday are from trials on 290 patients which were completed in July.
Glaxo Wellcome Plc dropped development of an oral version of Lexipafant for asthma in September on the grounds that it had little effect.
